summary: Frontend-only regression for iteration 19 covering the four Cloud Handoff / Vault enhancements. Activation (offline key) reached the studio. Cloud Send generated a 6-char share code + link + QR canvas (data-testid=cloud-qr) with working copy. The Library tab renders past sent handoffs with correct testids, Reopen triggered a receive and loaded cloud-received, copy-link works, and remove clears the row. Vault seed → open vault → rename via vault-rename-{id} → vault-rename-input-{id} → vault-rename-save-{id} updated the displayed name AND persisted across a full page reload. vault-edit-{id} opened the Track Editor modal (data-testid=track-editor-modal) titled 'Track Editor — Seed Take Editor' with expected 'Could not load this track for editing.' for the seed (no blob) — acceptable per spec. Expiry nudge (2 days) appeared with correct code/days text, expiry-reshare opened the Cloud Handoff modal, expiry-dismiss hid the bar and dismissal persisted after reload. No blocking console errors (only benign React hydration warning about <span> inside <option>).

ui_bugs.issue: When the same code exists in history for both directions (e.g. after Reopen on a code you sent, a 'received' entry with the same code is added), the row test-ids collide: two elements share data-testid='cloud-library-item-{CODE}' / cloud-library-remove-{CODE} / reopen / copy. Playwright strict-mode click fails without .first. React key uses `${dir}-${code}` so consider embedding dir into the data-testid too (e.g. cloud-library-remove-{dir}-{CODE}).
Modal exposes data-testid='track-editor-modal' but the review request/expected testid is 'track-editor'. Not blocking (both are self-consistent) but worth aligning docs or adding an alias.

action_items: Disambiguate library row test-ids by including direction: cloud-library-item-{dir}-{code} (and remove/reopen/copy siblings) so tools/tests can target sent vs received unambiguously.
Optional: alias track-editor-modal as track-editor (or update docs) for consistency with review spec.
critical_code_review_comments: cloudHistory.addHistory dedupes by (code+dir) only, so reopening a code you originally sent adds a duplicate 'received' entry — combined with (code)-only test-ids this causes the duplicate-testid issue above.
expiry-nudge logic (App.js L694-707) is clean; uses loadDismissed + <5 day window correctly and refreshes when the Cloud modal closes.
QR uses qrcode.react QRCodeCanvas inside div[data-testid=cloud-qr] — correctly renders a <canvas>.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for the 4 enhancements (all critical assertions passed)
